name: Red Sea, Yemen and Saudi Arabia
label: CRITICAL
key_judgment: Houthi missile and drone fire on Saudi Arabia will very likely continue at its current tempo, with the reopened Riyadh airport and the Yanbu-Rabigh export corridor the most probable targets; that corridor now carries Saudi crude rerouted away from Hormuz.
basis: The coalition said it intercepted three Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at the Eastern Province and four drones aimed at the south early on 27 October, after intercepting a Riyadh-bound missile on 26 October and saying it destroyed four launchers, five missile storage tunnels and a depot in Houthi territory. The Houthis claimed hits on King Khalid airport and oil pumping stations on 26 October; Riyadh has not confirmed either. Egypt's parliament authorised Sisi on 26 October, by a two-thirds vote, to support Saudi Arabia defensively, and a Houthi political bureau member called this a declaration of war on Yemen on 27 October. Israeli media, relayed by CTP-ISW, report an unverified $1 billion Saudi offer to the Houthis under an Iran-brokered deal. INTERTANKO notes no Houthi maritime operations for some time. Carrier suspensions run to mid-November for most European and Gulf airlines and to January 2027 for Cathay Pacific.
sponsor_posture: Houthis act with Iranian backing; Saudi Arabia and its coalition retaliate in Yemen.
cyber_nexus: Pro-Iran hacktivist personas target Gulf financial and government sites; Unit 42 reports Saudi ERP credential phishing and utility-bill scams. Egypt's authorisation of defensive support could add Egyptian banks and government portals to these personas' target set.
scenario: A Houthi strike closes Riyadh's airport for days during a regional leadership meeting, stranding staff, while phishing lures impersonate Saudi utility and payment portals.
so_what: Travel and staff safety in Saudi Arabia, Red Sea and Suez shipping insurance, and a second chokepoint on Gulf energy exports.
outlook: Next 72 hours: further Houthi salvos on Riyadh, the Eastern Province, the southern provinces and the East-West Pipeline corridor are very likely, with coalition strikes on Sanaa and the Red Sea coast continuing. Next 30 days: sustained pressure on Saudi airports and western export infrastructure is likely; an Egyptian deployment would likely stay defensive and limited, and Houthi action against Red Sea and Suez traffic in response to Egypt's move remains unlikely. The Tehran channel and the reported Saudi offer give a narrow route to restraint; carrier suspensions will likely run through November.

name: Strait of Hormuz and the Gulf
label: CRITICAL
key_judgment: Iran will very likely keep the strait effectively closed to unescorted traffic through at least the US midterms; verified merchant strikes continue at a low rate (22 and 23 October) as regional envoys press for a deal in Tehran, while US readiness for strikes on Iranian energy and military targets within 96 hours of an order makes a post-3 November escalation window likely.
basis: UKMTO verified on 26 October that an outbound tanker was disabled by a projectile in the strait on 23 October, the day after the Limah LPG strike, and on 26 October logged a vessel on fire 63 nm southeast of Al-Faw as suspicious activity. JMIC holds Hormuz at Severe and the wider Gulf at Substantial, citing five attacks inside the Gulf since 7 October. INTERTANKO counts more than 30 US-facilitated transits a day, about 90% tankers, against a pre-war baseline near 138, finds no credible evidence for Iranian mine claims and expects conditions to hold until the midterms. Iran's strait authority said on 27 October it will act against all Sinokor tankers, which carried nearly 40% of Hormuz crude last month, from 1 November. In Tehran, Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish envoys agreed on 26 October to continue talks; Iran lists seven US conditions and Qatari mediators are pursuing a five-day exchange of reopening for a blockade lift. DNI Clayton warned Iran is in advanced stages of planning attacks on US regional targets. Brent settled at $115.81 on 26 October and traded at $114.70 on 27 October.
sponsor_posture: Iran (IRGC Navy) is the principal; Tehran frames shipping attacks as leverage over US politics. The US holds the blockade and has pledged no strike on Iran before 3 November.
cyber_nexus: IRGC-linked CyberAv3ngers moved from Unitronics to Rockwell/Allen-Bradley controllers; Iran-linked intrusions hit US water utilities in 12+ states from late July; a UK power plant was shut for four days; about 60 hacktivist groups run DDoS and defacement. No new observed Iran-linked intrusion against US infrastructure was found for 25-27 October.
scenario: An IRGC-aligned persona claims a DDoS and data-leak operation against a US or Gulf payments brand during a spike in tanker attacks, while a separate actor probes internet-exposed OT at a facilities vendor.
so_what: Energy-cost and FX shock, Gulf staff and data-center continuity, and a higher chance of Iranian cyber activity against US financial and payment brands within days of kinetic events.
outlook: Next 72 hours: low-rate IRGC strikes and unverified claims against shipping likely continue, with the Tehran talks, Pezeshkian's Moscow visit and the 1 November PGSA deadline for Sinokor the main variables; a US strike before 3 November remains unlikely. Next 30 days: US readiness for large strikes after the midterms points to a post-3 November escalation window, which would likely bring IRGC action against shipping, Gulf bases and undersea cables unless the Qatari sequencing yields a transit bargain; enforcement against Sinokor would likely cut escorted crude flows sharply.

name: Afghanistan and Pakistan border
label: HIGH
key_judgment: Pakistan-Taliban border clashes and TTP-linked attacks inside Pakistan will likely continue; the failure of the Moscow talks removes the nearest diplomatic off-ramp.
basis: ISPR says six TTP militants and two soldiers were killed in Dera Ismail Khan's Zarkani area on 24 October. Pakistan's Foreign Office on 26 October rejected the Taliban's claim of 1,119 civilian casualties since 2022 and reaffirmed its right to self-defence, after a minister warned of all necessary measures if Afghan soil is used for attacks. On 25 October KP Governor Kundi confirmed the chief minister and speaker are under house arrest and said the 11 October emergency may run beyond six months; on 27 October a 48-member council was tasked with persuading militants to leave the 12 emergency districts through jirgas. The Taliban interior ministry on 27 October blamed Pakistan for drug smuggling. No new Kurram-Paktia exchange or mass-casualty attack was found between 18 and 27 October.
sponsor_posture: Pakistan's military; the Afghan Taliban; TTP and the IMP alliance.
scenario: A suicide attack on a Pakistani city disrupts staff travel and a regional processing center.
so_what: Staff safety in Pakistan; regional travel.
outlook: Next 72 hours: further ISPR-announced operations in southern KP and South Waziristan are likely, with TTP retaliation against police probable. Next 30 days: Islamabad's explicit warning of further action raises the likelihood of renewed Pakistani strikes into Afghanistan and Taliban border fire, with no diplomatic channel active.

name: Horn of Africa
label: HIGH
key_judgment: Ethiopia's federal offensive may be shifting toward a protracted counter-insurgency, a realistic possibility, as the TDF reoccupies vacated areas such as Rama and reportedly Abergele; an Ethiopia-Eritrea interstate war remains a realistic possibility while the border stays contested.
basis: No independently reported Tigray front-line change since the 22 October federal capture of Abiy Addi and Zana; TPF sources claim federal troops captured TPLF commander John Medid in Central Tigray on 26 October (unverified). On 25 October the ENDF chief of staff accused Eritrea and Egypt of backing the TPLF and claimed seizure of an arms shipment via Massawa, sustaining interstate rhetoric. In Somalia, Reuters reports dozens of soldiers killed in an al-Shabaab battle in Buurhakaba district around 26 October (al-Shabaab claims 321), while Laftagareen forces fought the army outside Baidoa and the Burhakabo push stalled at Leego. The Orthodox Synod reports more than 60 Christians killed in Arsi, Oromia, on 20 and 24 October.
sponsor_posture: Ethiopia; Eritrea and Egypt (accused by Addis of backing rebels); Somalia neutral.
scenario: Ethiopian strikes on Eritrean ports disrupt Red Sea traffic already diverted by the Hormuz closure.
so_what: Red Sea shipping, East African operations and staff; heightened risk to staff movement around Baidoa and Mogadishu approaches.
outlook: Next 72 hours: continued clashes in central and southern Tigray and further drone strikes; al-Shabaab and Laftagareen forces likely keep harassing the stalled federal column in Bay. Next 30 days: the Tigray war may shift to insurgency while Eritrean and Ethiopian rhetoric keeps interstate-war risk alive; the convergence of clan rebellion and al-Shabaab in Bay and Hiran likely erodes Mogadishu's southern positions.

name: Israel, Lebanon and Syria
label: HIGH
key_judgment: Israel-Hezbollah hostilities will likely continue at their current level through Israel's 27 October election, with a sharp escalation likely only if Hezbollah joins an Iranian attack.
basis: On 26 October, the eve of the election, Israel struck between Qantara and Bani Hayyan, carried out two major demolitions in Zawtar Sharqieh and shelled about a dozen south Lebanon localities, with one person hurt by unexploded ordnance; no Hezbollah fire into Israel was reported. Hezbollah signals are mixed: a senior official told al-Liwaa on 26 October the group has given no guarantee it will stay out of a war on Iran, while MP Fadlallah said Iran has not asked it to fight. Lebanese security sources told Reuters Iran has sent tens of millions of dollars for Hezbollah's military reconstitution. Voting opened on 27 October with 31.5% turnout at noon, the highest at that hour since 1973; the elections committee found no systematic tampering and Katz urged voters to back Netanyahu to finish the job in Iran. Check Point reports attacks on Israeli organisations up 55% year on year, with Handala tying its leaks to the vote and groups discussing election-day DoS against the Bank of Israel and ministries.
sponsor_posture: Iran backs Hezbollah; Israel's posture hardens before its election.
cyber_nexus: Handala (MOIS-linked) ties its leak operations to the Israeli election; Check Point counts about 2,700 attacks a week on Israeli organisations, with election-day DoS discussed against the Bank of Israel.
scenario: A Hezbollah decision to join an Iranian strike triggers Israeli strikes on Beirut's southern suburbs and a regional flight shutdown.
so_what: Staff and vendor exposure in Israel and Lebanon; Israeli technology suppliers as targets of Iranian data-leak operations.
outlook: Next 72 hours: continued Israeli strikes and demolitions in south Lebanon and incursions in Quneitra through the count and its immediate aftermath, with hacktivist DoS and Handala leak claims likely to continue around the results. Next 30 days: coalition bargaining after the vote is unlikely to change Israel's posture in Lebanon or Syria; the main escalation path runs through a post-midterm US or Israeli strike on Iran, where Hezbollah's ambiguous position and Iranian-funded reconstitution raise the chance it joins.

name: Russia and Ukraine
label: HIGH
key_judgment: Reciprocal energy-infrastructure attacks will very likely continue into the winter; both sides confirm only a technical round in Abu Dhabi in the first half of November, Zelensky counts more than 170 Russian energy strikes since the 11 October ceasefire call, and no energy truce is in view.
basis: Russia fired 16 ballistic missiles and more than 280 drones overnight into 27 October, mainly at Kyiv, killing one, closing the Pivdennyi Bridge and disrupting the Green metro line; Zelensky says most targets were energy, logistics and urban infrastructure. A drone cut power to part of Chernivtsi on 26 October and Ukrenergo reported outages in six regions. Zelensky says Ukraine received 24 US Patriot interceptors in 90 days. Ukrainian drones killed two in Bryansk and one on a bus in occupied Zaporizhzhia on 27 October; the General Staff claims hits on the Energiya (Yelets) and Proton-Electrotex (Oryol) microelectronics plants. Russia claims a strike on a cargo ship bound for Chornomorsk. The Oleshky local ceasefire began on 27 October, while Peskov says talks imply no limits on military operations.
sponsor_posture: Russia escalates against Ukraine's grid; Ukraine targets Russian fuel revenue. US-Ukraine relations are strained.
cyber_nexus: Sandworm-class operators have a long record against Ukrainian energy; pro-Russian DDoS crews (NoName057(16)) target European governments and banks.
scenario: A wiper hits a Ukrainian distribution operator during a cold snap and spreads to a European subsidiary through a shared IT provider.
so_what: European energy prices, sanctions-compliance load, and DDoS against European financial sites.
outlook: Next 72 hours: continued Russian missile and drone raids on generation, substations and Kyiv logistics, and Ukrainian long-range strikes on Russian defence-industrial and petrochemical targets; Oleshky compliance through about 31 October is the near-term test. Next 30 days: a trilateral round after 4 November, where an energy truce is on the table for Kyiv; a strike disabling a major Russian export terminal would argue for CRITICAL.

name: Sahel and West Africa
label: HIGH
key_judgment: JNIM will likely keep pressure on central Mali garrisons and Bamako's fuel supply, while its war with Islamic State Sahel Province spreads toward Niger and Nigeria; the army's return to Kidal does not reduce pressure in the centre.
basis: No new major attack in Mali, Burkina Faso or Niger was found for 25-27 October; the latest confirmed events remain the 18-19 October IS Sahel massacre near Menaka (54 bodies found at Tagadayat, per the army on 24 October) and Niger's 25 October overnight petrol-sales ban. In Nigeria, the toll from the 23 October raid on Binnari, Taraba State, rose to at least 62 dead (AP, NEMA). Goïta is due at the third Russia-Africa summit in Moscow on 28-29 October. No new reporting on the Bamako fuel blockade or attacks on Bamako.
sponsor_posture: JNIM (al-Qaeda); FLA separatists; Russian Africa Corps supports the junta.
scenario: A renewed blockade of Bamako forces evacuation of regional staff and suspends payment-network services in Mali.
so_what: Staff and agent networks in Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger.
outlook: Next 72 hours: Moscow summit announcements on Russian security support to the AES are likely; further army strikes around Menaka and possible ISSP reprisals. Next 30 days: JNIM-ISSP fighting in the tri-border area and attacks in northern Nigeria likely continue; regional fuel stress in Mali and Niger bears watching.

name: Sudan
label: HIGH
key_judgment: Sudan's war will likely intensify over the next 30 days without talks, with mass-casualty drone strikes on towns, attacks on power and water infrastructure, and growing spillover into Abyei and Chad.
basis: A day after the 26 October coordinated RSF drone strikes on power stations in Al-Jazira, Gedaref, White Nile and Sennar, a drone hit the Al-Markhiyat transformer station in Khartoum early on 27 October, cutting power across much of Khartoum and Al-Jazira (AFP; electricity company source blames the RSF). A drone strike on a Nyala market on the evening of 26 October killed 21 people, a hospital medic told AFP, which did not attribute it; army sources claim strikes that night destroyed RSF command sites and air defences near Nyala airport. On 26 October the foreign ministry rejected famine warnings from 32 countries and argued a truce would let the RSF regroup. No talks are in view.
sponsor_posture: SAF (backed by Egypt); RSF (external backing alleged).
scenario: Sustained drone strikes on Khartoum and eastern substations knock out power and telecoms, cutting payment acceptance and correspondent-banking connectivity in army-held Sudan.
so_what: Humanitarian payments and sanctions screening; regional staff.
outlook: Next 72 hours: further RSF drone strikes on grid and fuel sites in Khartoum and army-held states, and continued army strikes on Nyala, Ed Daein and El Fasher. Next 30 days: infrastructure attacks likely widen outages in the capital and the east, while the Abyei dispute and Chad border strikes sustain spillover risk.

name: Europe: hybrid threats and sabotage
label: ELEVATED
key_judgment: Russian-directed sabotage will likely keep targeting the Starlink and space-ground network supporting Ukraine, alongside defence-industrial and logistics sites, below the Article 5 threshold, while Iranian intelligence will likely keep plotting against Jewish communities and, on UK police assessment, US-used military sites in Europe.
basis: Romania's SRI and DIICOT said on 26 October that a Russia-coordinated network of two Belarusians and a Ukrainian set the 14 September fire beside ROMARM's Carfil plant in Brasov; two have been arrested and were allegedly preparing similar attacks in Germany, and a warrant was issued for the third, believed to be in Poland. A European Parliamentary Research Service briefing (26 October) records Russia-linked cyber activity in nine member states, including Cyprus and Polish heat and power plants. Sikorski attributed the hybrid campaign to a GRU unit on 26 October; Moscow promised a tough response to Moldova's expulsion of a Russian diplomat; no new Black Sea ship strike off Romania or Bulgaria was found for 25-27 October.
sponsor_posture: Russia (GRU-directed proxies, often recruited online); Iran (criminal proxies).
cyber_nexus: NoName057(16) pays volunteers in crypto for DDoS; hacktivist DDoS follows political events within days.
scenario: A recruited proxy sets fire to a logistics hub that hosts a payments data-center cage, while a DDoS wave hits the same country's banks.
so_what: Physical security at European data and logistics sites, executive protection, and DDoS readiness for European services.
outlook: Next 72 hours: further drone strikes on merchant shipping in the western Black Sea, a possible Russian retaliatory step against Moldova, and further detail on the Brasov network's other attacks. Next 30 days: the Bulgarian runoff on 1 November, attacks or arrests linked to Starlink ground stations and defence suppliers, and pro-Russian DDoS; a third fatal strike in Romanian waters or an armed drone crossing into NATO territory would argue for HIGH.

name: Korean Peninsula and DPRK revenue operations
label: ELEVATED
key_judgment: DPRK border pressure is rising, with self-propelled artillery exposed opposite Gimpo and a UN letter warning of self-defence measures; a border incident is the main near-term risk, a near-term ICBM or nuclear test remains less likely during APEC diplomacy, and revenue operations remain the most direct state threat to financial firms.
basis: On 26-27 October Reuters, SBS and NK News observed North Korean 122mm self-propelled howitzers at two western border locations opposite Gimpo, with fortification work continuing; on 27 October South Korea's JCS assessed them as legacy artillery deployed in plain view and said they cannot be considered the new tactical weapons Kim Yo Jong threatened. Deepfakes exaggerating the deployment circulated widely the same week. KCNA reported a DPRK letter to the UN Security Council warning of self-defence measures. Switzerland's foreign minister is due in Pyongyang from 29 October to open a political office. OFAC delisted three SEK Studio-linked Chinese parties on 21 October without explanation. No ballistic launch has been reported since 12 October, loudspeaker activation had not been reported through 27 October, and no new DPRK-attributed theft or IT-worker case was found for 23-27 October.
sponsor_posture: DPRK (RGB); revenue crime runs as statecraft.
cyber_nexus: APT38 / Lazarus target exchanges, bridges and banks; IT workers recruited through third-country fronts.
scenario: A remote engineer hired through a staffing vendor, fronted by a third-country 'interview associate', exfiltrates source code and API keys for a payments platform.
so_what: Hiring and contractor identity proofing, crypto and settlement infrastructure, and sanctions exposure from DPRK payments.
outlook: Next 72 hours: loudspeaker activation before end-October remains likely, and Seoul's proportionate response alongside exposed DPRK artillery makes a border incident the main risk. Next 30 days: a launch around the end of Hoguk or Keen Sword remains possible while APEC diplomacy may restrain larger tests; Lazarus laundering of Drift and Bitget proceeds and PHP2Shell exploitation remain the financial-sector cyber risk.

name: Mexico and the US cartel campaign
label: ELEVATED
key_judgment: US military pressure on cartels will likely widen from maritime strikes to land targets in Latin America within months, raising retaliation risk and sanctions-screening load in Mexico.
basis: Sheinbaum answered the NYT-reported US memo on 26 October, saying Mexico coordinates with Washington but will not accept US forces on its territory and that such requests have recurred under Trump. No new US boat strike was found after the 4 October Caribbean strike, and OFAC listed no cartel designations through 26 October. Mexican forces arrested Los Rusos operator 'El Isra' in Mexicali on 26 October; Noroeste counted 42 violent deaths in Sinaloa in the week to 25 October, 5% below the prior week. A Canacar-led national trucker strike on 26 October over highway insecurity and extortion blocked several federal highways without a deal.
sponsor_posture: US military and Treasury; Mexican cartels designated as FTOs in February 2025.
cyber_nexus: Cartels use drones for surveillance and attack; financial networks span racing, construction, trucking and fuel.
scenario: A US strike on a cartel facility triggers retaliation against foreign businesses in Sinaloa, and OFAC adds front companies that appear in merchant portfolios.
so_what: Merchant and correspondent-bank sanctions screening in Mexico; staff safety in Sinaloa and Tamaulipas; road-freight disruption and cargo-security exposure for clients with Mexican supply chains while the trucker strike lasts.
outlook: Next 72 hours: whether the trucker strike persists and how Washington responds to Sheinbaum's public refusal. Next 30 days: pre-midterm pressure (3 November) raises the odds of a resumed boat strike, a first land action or new OFAC designations.

name: South China Sea and Luzon Strait
label: ELEVATED
key_judgment: China-Philippines friction will likely continue at sea, with the next Sierra Madre rotation the most probable flashpoint; the ASEAN summit in Manila and APEC diplomacy argue for restraint over the next three weeks.
basis: The AFP counted 54 Chinese vessels at West Philippine Sea features for 20-26 October, up from 31 the prior week, excluding the PLAN Liaoning group that Trinidad said passed within 15 miles of Philippine landmass before exiting south (27 Oct). On 25 October the PCG expelled a foreign fishing vessel from Pag-asa's territorial sea while CCG 21581 and two RHIBs trailed it, without interference. The DFA on 26 October denied any subsea-cable arrangement with Taiwan, walking back a diplomat's Bashi Channel remarks. Manila hosts the ADMM and ADMM-Plus in Cebu on 28-29 October with Hegseth expected; China's attendance is unconfirmed and its foreign ministry warned on 26 October against attempts to 'hijack ASEAN'. No ramming, water-cannon or Sierra Madre incident was found for 24-27 October.
sponsor_posture: PRC (CCG, maritime militia, PLA Southern Theater Command).
cyber_nexus: Chinese state groups run espionage against Philippine and Southeast Asian government networks (the 8 October multinational advisory on Integrity Technology Group cited Southeast Asian email theft); no new Philippine-specific cyber item found for 24-27 October.
scenario: A collision at Second Thomas Shoal kills a Filipino sailor, invoking the US-Philippines treaty and disrupting shipping through the Luzon Strait.
so_what: Undersea-cable and shipping routes through the Luzon Strait; Manila operations centers.
outlook: Next 72 hours: the ADMM-Plus in Cebu (28-29 October) and a Hegseth-Teodoro bilateral are the focal events; Chinese criticism of US-Philippine statements there is likely, and a CCG show of presence at Scarborough or Second Thomas is possible. Next 30 days: the ASEAN summit in Manila (15-17 November) and Marcos's APEC trip to China argue for restraint, with the next Sierra Madre rotation the most likely flashpoint.

name: Taiwan Strait
label: ELEVATED
key_judgment: PLA pressure on Taiwan will likely stay below blockade over the next 30 days, but CCG jurisdiction claims at Pratas are the most probable route to a boarding or inspection precedent; a named joint exercise remains the warning sign of a step change.
basis: Taiwan MND detected 3 PLA aircraft sorties (1 across the median line), 6 PLAN ships and 9 official ships in the 24 hours to 06:00 on 26 October, the first aircraft after four days without any during Typhoon Champi; the 27 October report was not yet posted at review time. The CGA said on 24 October that China is pairing maritime militia boats with coast guard ships for 'battlefield preparation' around Taiwan and into the western Pacific, with activity up since June. The PLA Eastern Theater Command marked Beijing's 25 October Taiwan Recovery Day with a propaganda poster and no exercise. A national-security source said on 27 October that Beijing is pressuring entertainers and firms linked to Taipei mayoral candidate Puma Shen. No named exercise and no new CCG incident at Pratas, Kinmen or Penghu was found for 24-27 October.
sponsor_posture: PRC (PLA Eastern Theater Command, China Coast Guard).
cyber_nexus: Flax Typhoon infrastructure seized by the US; Salt Typhoon remains inside telecom carriers; The Gentlemen hit a Taiwanese manufacturer.
scenario: A named PLA exercise announces inspection zones east of Taiwan; shipping and air routes divert; Taiwan-based semiconductor suppliers delay deliveries.
so_what: Semiconductor supply chain, Asia-Pacific routing of traffic and staff, and Chinese espionage against telecom-dependent authentication.
outlook: Next 72 hours: sortie counts likely return toward pre-typhoon levels of 10 to 30 a day, with CCG patrols resuming around Pratas. Next 30 days: watch for a named exercise and intensified influence and cyber operations ahead of Taiwan's late-November local elections, and further CCG jurisdiction claims around Pratas and Penghu.

name: Central Asia
label: GUARDED
key_judgment: The theater holds at its baseline: reporting from August to October shows isolated border incidents without escalation, with the Tajik-Afghan border the main watch point.
basis: No Tajik-Afghan border incident, ISKP attack or unrest was found for 23-27 October. Ukraine's I Want to Live project says more than 20,400 Central Asians had signed Russian military contracts by 1 October, an unverified figure. Earlier reporting on Chinese pressure on Tajikistan, the Taliban road to the Wakhan border and ISKP activity in northern Afghanistan stands.
sponsor_posture: Russia and China compete for influence.
outlook: Next 72 hours: baseline. Next 30 days: the Tajik-Afghan border and ISKP in northern Afghanistan remain the watch points; coverage remains thin.

name: South Asia: India and Pakistan
label: GUARDED
key_judgment: India-Pakistan rhetoric is sharp but no mobilization indicator is observed; a mass-casualty attack in India attributed to a Pakistan-based group would very likely trigger cross-border strikes, as in 2025.
basis: No Line of Control ceasefire violation, infiltration bid or mass-casualty attack in India was found for 23-27 October. Pakistan's 27 October Kashmir Black Day statements by President Zardari, PM Sharif and FM Dar called for a peaceful, UN-based resolution and carried no threat of force. Pakistan's Foreign Office said on 23 October that war is not a solution, and India's civil defence training plan announced on 24 October is preparatory. Deterrent rhetoric on the Indus Waters Treaty from 21 October stands without a new Indian reply.
sponsor_posture: Indian and Pakistani militaries; Pakistan-based militant groups.
cyber_nexus: Pakistan- and India-aligned hacktivists deface news sites during crises.
scenario: A mass-casualty attack in an Indian city triggers missile strikes and airspace closures; operations centers in India lose staff access for days.
so_what: Large Indian operations and technology centers; regional airspace and connectivity.
outlook: Next 72 hours: no change expected. Next 30 days: escalation still depends on a triggering attack in Jammu and Kashmir or elsewhere in India; watch for an Indian response on the Indus Waters Treaty.

name: Venezuela and the Caribbean
label: GUARDED
key_judgment: Venezuela's US-backed transition will likely continue without major violence over the next 30 days; the 22 October nationwide protest passed peacefully, leaving the absent election date and the opposition split as the main pressure points.
basis: Machado's 25 October return passed without violence, and Vente Venezuela announced a national tour to press for elections. Interim president Delcy Rodríguez on 26 October called the return a 'show' and denied political persecution, while Rubio said the same day that street protest would not deliver democracy and set a new Supreme Court, a new electoral council and a debt resolution as prerequisites, with no date. The IACHR reminded Caracas on 27 October of its duty to protect Machado. No US military activity in the Caribbean or boat strike was found for 22-27 October.
sponsor_posture: US-backed interim government under Delcy Rodríguez; Washington publicly prioritises an institution-first sequence over Machado's 2027 election push.
scenario: Sanctions relief opens new correspondent-banking flows that criminal networks try to exploit.
so_what: Sanctions-screening changes and new payment corridors.
outlook: Next 72 hours: Machado's first tour stops and any detentions of Vente organisers; watch whether Washington and Machado narrow or widen their public gap on timing. Next 30 days: the fourth round of talks on 11-15 November and the election date remain the pressure points.

name: Western Balkans
label: GUARDED
key_judgment: Vucic's concession on election night removes the disputed-result scenario; government formation and the SNS handover will likely pass without sustained unrest, with isolated clashes possible and north Kosovo below violence.
basis: CRTA's 26 October preliminary assessment projects 52.45% and 138 seats for the Student List against 39.2% for Vucic's list, consistent with his 25 October concession; it frames the vote as mobilization against electoral engineering, after recording ballot photographing at 48% of stations. AFP reported celebrations without violence. No incident in north Kosovo was found for 25-27 October.
cyber_nexus: Russian influence operations in Serbia and Republika Srpska.
scenario: A bridge-area clash prompts KFOR to return and Serbia to raise its alert level.
outlook: Next 72 hours: official results from the electoral commission; isolated local friction is possible but a contested result looks unlikely. Next 30 days: government formation and a handover from SNS, with risk of friction in state institutions; a reversal of the concession or clashes in north Kosovo would argue for a return to ELEVATED.
